summary: Ten kinds of family groups came up from Bavel with Ezra. This mishnah teaches which groups may marry each other.

chunks.en: Ten kinds of families came up from Bavel:
chunks.st: There were ten categories of lineage, with varying restrictions on marriage, among the Jews who ascended from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael with Ezra before the building of the Second Temple. They are as follows:

chunks.en: Kohanim, Leviim,
chunks.st: Priests; Levites;

chunks.en: Yisraelim, chalalim,
chunks.st: Israelites; priests disqualified due to flawed lineage [ḥalalim];

words.note: Children of Kohanim who lost their Kohen status because of their family.

chunks.en: gerim, and freed servants,
chunks.st: converts, and emancipated slaves;

words.note: People who joined the Jewish people.

chunks.en: mamzerim, nesinim,
chunks.st: mamzerim; Gibeonites, i.e., the descendants of the Gibeonites who converted in the time of Joshua;

words.note: From the Givonim, who joined in the days of Yehoshua.

chunks.en: shtukim, and asufim.
chunks.st: children of unknown paternity [shetuki]; and foundlings.

words.note: People whose father is not known.
Babies found with no known parents.

chunks.en: Kohanim, Leviim, and Yisraelim
chunks.st: The mishna proceeds to detail their halakhot: With regard to priests, Levites, and Israelites,

chunks.en: may marry each other.
chunks.st: it is permitted for men and women in these categories to marry one another.

chunks.en: Leviim, Yisraelim,
chunks.st: With regard to Levites who are not priests, Israelites,

chunks.en: chalalim, gerim, and freed servants
chunks.st: ḥalalim, converts, and emancipated slaves,

chunks.en: may marry each other.
chunks.st: it is permitted for men and women in these categories to marry one another.

chunks.en: Gerim and freed servants,
chunks.st: With regard to converts, and emancipated slaves,

chunks.en: mamzerim, nesinim, shtukim, and asufim,
chunks.st: mamzerim, and Gibeonites, children of unknown paternity [shetuki], and foundlings,

chunks.en: may all marry each other.
chunks.st: it is permitted for all of the men and women in these categories to marry one another.

summary: This mishnah explains who is a shtuki and who is an asufi.

chunks.en: And these are the shtukim:
chunks.st: And these are the last two categories:

chunks.en: anyone who knows his mother
chunks.st: A shetuki is any person who knows the identity of his mother

chunks.en: but does not know his father.
chunks.st: but does not know the identity of his father.

chunks.en: Asufim: anyone who was picked up from the marketplace
chunks.st: A foundling is anyone who was collected from the marketplace

chunks.he: וְאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר לֹא אָבִיו וְלֹא אִמּוֹ.
chunks.en: and does not know his father or his mother.
chunks.st: and doesn’t know the identity of his parents, neither that of his father nor that of his mother.
chunks.stMore: These two categories are people whose status is uncertain; they may be mamzerim.

chunks.he: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל הָיָה קוֹרֵא לִשְׁתוּקֵי, בְּדוּקֵי:
chunks.en: Abba Shaul would call shtukim "beduki."
chunks.explain: Beduki means "checked": we can ask his mother about the father.
chunks.st: Abba Shaul would call a shetuki by the label of beduki.
chunks.basisNote: The meaning of "beduki" comes from Bartenura.

summary: People who may not marry into the regular Jewish community may marry each other. Rabbi Yehuda forbids this, and Rabbi Eliezer forbids marriage where there is a doubt.

chunks.en: All those who may not marry into the community
chunks.st: All those for whom it is prohibited to enter into the congregation, i.e., to marry a Jew of unflawed lineage,

chunks.en: may marry each other.
chunks.st: are permitted to marry into each other’s families.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda forbids it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda prohibits them from marrying anyone other than those who share their specific flaw.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: definite ones with definite ones is allowed.
chunks.explain: Definite means we know for sure about their family.
chunks.st: It is permitted for those with definite flaws to marry with those with definite flaws. For example, it is permitted for mamzerim and Gibeonites to marry each other.

chunks.en: But definite ones with doubtful ones,
chunks.st: By contrast, it is prohibited for those with definite flaws, such as mamzerim, to marry with those whose flaws result from an uncertainty, such as a child of unknown paternity [shetuki] and a foundling;

chunks.en: or doubtful ones with definite ones,
chunks.st: and it is prohibited for those whose flaws result from an uncertainty to marry with those with definite flaws;

chunks.en: or doubtful ones with doubtful ones, is forbidden.
chunks.st: and it is prohibited for those whose flaws result from an uncertainty to marry with those whose flaws result from an uncertainty, such as a shetuki and a female shetuki.

chunks.en: And these are the doubtful ones:
chunks.st: And these are the ones whose flaws result from an uncertainty:

chunks.en: a shtuki, an asufi, and a Kusi.
chunks.st: A shetuki, a foundling, and a Samaritan.

words.note: A Shomroni; their status as Jews was in doubt.

summary: A Kohen who marries a woman must check her family going back several generations to be sure it is fit for a Kohen.

chunks.en: A Kohen who marries a Kohen's daughter
chunks.st: A priest who marries a woman who is the daughter of a priest

chunks.en: must check her family,
chunks.st: must investigate with regard to her background, i.e., he must check previous generations of her family tree from both the maternal and paternal sides,

chunks.en: four mothers, which are eight:
chunks.st: for four mothers, which are eight.

chunks.en: her mother, and her mother's mother,
chunks.st: How so? He investigates the lineage of her mother, and the mother of her mother,

chunks.en: and her mother's father's mother, and that one's mother,
chunks.st: and the mother of her mother’s father, and her mother, i.e., the mother of her mother’s fathers’ mother.

chunks.en: and her father's mother and that one's mother,
chunks.st: And he also investigates the lineage of the mother of her father, and her mother, i.e., the mother of her father’s mother,

chunks.en: and her father's father's mother and that one's mother.
chunks.st: and the mother of her father’s father, and her mother i.e., the mother of her father’s father’s mother.

chunks.en: For a Levi's daughter or a Yisrael's daughter,
chunks.st: If he seeks to marry a Levite woman or an Israelite woman,

chunks.en: we add one more.
chunks.st: he adds to these an investigation of mothers of one additional generation.

summary: Some families do not need to be checked, because someone in them already held a job that only people from a fit family could get.

chunks.he: אֵין בּוֹדְקִין לֹא מִן הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּלְמַעְלָה,
chunks.en: We do not check past someone who served at the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: With regard to these investigations, one need not investigate from the altar and above.
chunks.stMore: If his ancestors included a priest who served at the altar, one checks no further, as the court would have investigated his lineage before allowing him to participate in the Temple service.

chunks.en: and not past a Levi who sang on the duchan,
chunks.st: Nor do they check from the platform, used by Levites for singing in the Temple, and above,

words.note: The platform where the Leviim sang.

chunks.en: and not past a member of the Sanhedrin.
chunks.st: nor from the Sanhedrin and above,
chunks.stMore: since only one whose lineage has been examined and who was found to be fit can be appointed to the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: And anyone whose fathers were known
chunks.st: And similarly, anyone whose ancestors

chunks.en: as public officers,
chunks.st: held public posts,

chunks.en: or tzedakah collectors,
chunks.st: and anyone whose ancestors were charity collectors,

chunks.en: may marry into Kehunah,
chunks.st: may marry into the priesthood,

chunks.en: and there is no need to check them.
chunks.st: and there is no need to investigate their lineage,
chunks.stMore: since no one of flawed lineage would be appointed to those positions.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: also someone who signed as a witness
chunks.st: Even the descendants of one who had signed as a witness

chunks.en: in the old court of Tzippori.
chunks.st: in the old court [ba’arki] of Tzippori do not need to have their lineage investigated.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

chunks.en: also someone who was written
chunks.st: Even the descendants of one who was written

chunks.en: in the king's army list.
chunks.st: in the army list [be’isteratya] of the Jewish king do not need to have their lineage investigated.

summary: The daughter of a chalal may never marry a Kohen. It depends on whether the father or the mother was the chalal. Rabbi Yehuda says the same about a ger's daughter.

chunks.en: The daughter of a male chalal
chunks.st: The daughter of a male ḥalal

chunks.en: may never marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: is unfit to marry into the priesthood forever.
chunks.stMore: In other words, all daughters of male descendants of a ḥalal are prohibited from marrying priests, as they have the status of ḥalalot.

chunks.en: A Yisrael who married a chalalah,
chunks.st: If there was an Israelite who married a ḥalala,

chunks.en: his daughter may marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is fit to marry into the priesthood,

chunks.en: A chalal who married a Yisrael's daughter,
chunks.st: whereas if there was a ḥalal who married a Jewish woman,

chunks.en: his daughter may not marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is unfit to marry into the priesthood.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: בַּת גֵּר זָכָר כְּבַת חָלָל זָכָר:
chunks.en: the daughter of a male ger is like the daughter of a male chalal.
chunks.st: The daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male ḥalal, and she is also prohibited from marrying into the priesthood.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says a girl may marry a Kohen if one of her parents was born Jewish. Rabbi Yosei says even a daughter of two gerim may.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov disagrees and says:

chunks.en: A Yisrael who married a giyores,
chunks.st: If there was an Israelite who married a female convert,

words.note: A woman who joined the Jewish people.

chunks.en: his daughter may marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is fit to marry into the priesthood,

chunks.en: And a ger who married a Yisrael's daughter,
chunks.st: and similarly if there was a convert who married a Jewish woman,

chunks.en: his daughter may marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is fit to marry into the priesthood.

chunks.en: But a ger who married a giyores,
chunks.st: But if there was a male convert who married a female convert,

chunks.en: his daughter may not marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is unfit to marry into the priesthood.

chunks.en: The same for gerim and freed servants,
chunks.st: With regard to both converts and emancipated Canaanite slaves,

chunks.en: even up to ten generations,
chunks.st: their daughters are unfit to marry into the priesthood even up to ten generations.

chunks.en: until the mother is from Yisrael.
chunks.st: This halakha applies to the offspring until his mother is born Jewish.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: even a ger who married a giyores,
chunks.st: Even if there was a male convert who married a female convert,

chunks.en: his daughter may marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is fit to marry into the priesthood.

summary: A father is not believed to say his son is a mamzer. Rabbi Yehuda says parents are believed about a baby that is not born yet.

chunks.en: If someone says, This son of mine is a mamzer,
chunks.st: One who says: This son of mine is a mamzer,
chunks.stMore: e.g., if he claims that the son was born to one forbidden to him by a prohibition that carries the punishment of karet,

chunks.en: he is not believed.
chunks.st: he is not deemed credible to render him a mamzer.

chunks.en: And even if both of them say
chunks.st: And even if both of them, the father and the mother, admit

chunks.en: about the baby she is expecting that it is a mamzer,
chunks.st: that a fetus in her womb is a mamzer,

chunks.en: they are not believed.
chunks.st: they are not deemed credible.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says, they are believed.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: They are deemed credible.

summary: If a father sent a messenger to make kiddushin for his daughter and also did it himself, whichever came first counts. The same is true for a woman and her messenger.

chunks.en: Someone who gave permission to his messenger
chunks.st: In a case of one who authorized his agent

chunks.en: to make kiddushin for his daughter,
chunks.st: to betroth his daughter to a man that the agent would deem fit,

chunks.en: and he himself went and made kiddushin for her,
chunks.st: and the father went and betrothed her to someone else,

chunks.en: if his came first,
chunks.st: if his betrothal preceded that of the agent,

chunks.en: his kiddushin counts.
chunks.st: his betrothal is a valid betrothal;

chunks.en: And if his messenger's came first,
chunks.st: and if the betrothal of his agent preceded his own,

chunks.en: the messenger's kiddushin counts.
chunks.st: the betrothal of the agent is a valid betrothal.

chunks.en: And if it is not known,
chunks.st: And if it is not known whose betrothal came first,

chunks.en: both of them give a get.
chunks.st: both men who might have betrothed her give her a bill of divorce in order to render her permitted to marry someone else.

chunks.en: And if they want,
chunks.st: And if they wish and agree between them,

chunks.en: one gives a get and the other marries her.
chunks.st: one gives a bill of divorce and the other marries her.

chunks.he: וְכֵן הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנָּתְנָה רְשׁוּת לִשְׁלוּחָהּ לְקַדְּשָׁהּ,
chunks.en: And the same for a woman who gave permission to her messenger to make kiddushin for her,
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to a woman who authorized her agent to betroth her

chunks.en: and she went and made kiddushin herself,
chunks.st: and she then went and betrothed herself to someone else,

chunks.en: if hers came first,
chunks.st: if her own betrothal preceded that of the agent,

chunks.en: her kiddushin counts.
chunks.st: her betrothal is a valid betrothal,

chunks.en: And if her messenger's came first,
chunks.st: and if that of her agent preceded hers,

chunks.en: his kiddushin counts.
chunks.st: the agent’s betrothal is a valid betrothal.

chunks.en: And if it is not known,
chunks.st: And if they do not know whose betrothal came first,

chunks.en: both of them give her a get.
chunks.st: both men who may have betrothed her give her a bill of divorce.

chunks.en: And if they want,
chunks.st: And if they wish,

chunks.he: אֶחָד נוֹתֵן לָהּ גֵּט וְאֶחָד כּוֹנֵס:
chunks.en: one gives her a get and the other marries her.
chunks.st: one may give a bill of divorce and the other marries her.

summary: If a man went far away with his wife and came back with her and children, he does not need to prove who they are. If his wife died there, he must prove only that the children are hers.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁיָּצָא הוּא וְאִשְׁתּוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
chunks.en: Someone who went overseas with his wife,
chunks.st: With regard to one who went overseas with his wife,

chunks.en: and came back with his wife and children,
chunks.st: and returned with his wife and children,

chunks.he: וְאָמַר, אִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּצָאת עִמִּי לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
chunks.en: and said: This woman who went overseas with me,
chunks.st: and said: This is the woman who went overseas with me

chunks.en: here she is, and these are her children,
chunks.st: and these are her children,

chunks.en: he does not need to bring proof,
chunks.st: he is not required to bring proof

chunks.he: לֹא עַל הָאִשָּׁה וְלֹא עַל הַבָּנִים.
chunks.en: not about the woman and not about the children.
chunks.st: with regard to the lineage of the woman, since her lineage was already investigated at the time of their marriage, nor with regard to the lineage of the children.

chunks.en: If she died, and these are her children,
chunks.st: If he returned without the woman and said: My wife died and these are her children,

chunks.en: he brings proof about the children,
chunks.st: he must bring proof that the children were born to his wife,

chunks.en: but he does not bring proof about the woman.
chunks.st: but he does not need to bring proof with regard to the lineage of the woman.

summary: If a man married a woman far away and came back with her and children, he must prove her family is fit. If she died there, he must prove about her and the children.

chunks.en: I married a woman overseas,
chunks.st: If he left when he was unmarried and said upon his return: I married a woman overseas,

chunks.en: and this is she, and these are her children,
chunks.st: and this is she, and these are her children,

chunks.en: he brings proof about the woman,
chunks.st: he must bring proof with regard to the lineage of the woman,

chunks.he: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה עַל הַבָּנִים.
chunks.en: and he does not need to bring proof about the children.
chunks.st: but he is not required to bring proof with regard to the lineage of the children.

chunks.en: She died, and these are her children,
chunks.st: If he said: I married a woman overseas and she died, and these are her children,

chunks.en: he needs to bring proof
chunks.st: he is required to bring proof

chunks.en: about the woman and about the children.
chunks.st: with regard to both the lineage of the woman and the children.

summary: This mishnah teaches the rules of yichud: when a man and a woman may not be alone together, and when it is allowed, like with his own wife, mother, or daughter.

chunks.he: לֹא יִתְיַחֵד אָדָם עִם שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים,
chunks.en: A man may not be alone with two women,
chunks.explain: Being alone together is called yichud.
chunks.st: A man may not be secluded with two women lest he sin with them,

chunks.en: but one woman may be alone
chunks.st: but one woman may be secluded

chunks.en: with two men.
chunks.st: with two men.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: אַף אִישׁ אֶחָד מִתְיַחֵד עִם שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
chunks.en: Even one man may be alone with two women
chunks.st: Even one man may be secluded with two women

chunks.en: when his wife is with him,
chunks.st: when his wife is with him,

chunks.en: and he may sleep with them at an inn,
chunks.st: and in that situation he may even sleep in the same inn with two women,

chunks.en: because his wife watches over him.
chunks.st: because his wife guards him from sinning with them.

chunks.he: מִתְיַחֵד אָדָם עִם אִמּוֹ וְעִם בִּתּוֹ,
chunks.en: A man may be alone with his mother and with his daughter,
chunks.st: They further said that a man may be secluded with his mother, and with his daughter,

chunks.en: and sleep close to them.
chunks.st: and sleep alongside them with bodily contact without clothes, since there is no concern that they will engage in sexual intercourse.

chunks.en: And when they grow up,
chunks.st: And when they, the son or daughter, have grown up,

chunks.he: זוֹ יְשֵׁנָה בִכְסוּתָהּ וְזֶה יָשֵׁן בִּכְסוּתוֹ:
chunks.en: she sleeps in her own clothes and he sleeps in his own clothes.
chunks.st: this one sleeps in her garment and that one sleeps in his garment, but they may share a bed.

summary: This mishnah teaches who should not be a teacher of young children.

chunks.en: A man who is not married should not be a teacher of children,
chunks.st: A bachelor may not act as a teacher of children,

chunks.en: and a woman should not be a teacher of children.
chunks.st: nor may a woman act as a teacher of children.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: even someone who does not have a wife with him
chunks.st: Even one who does not have a wife

chunks.en: should not be a teacher of children.
chunks.st: may not act as a teacher of children.

summary: The Sages teach which jobs a father should teach his son, and that a living comes from Hashem, not from the job. Rabbi Nehorai says he teaches his son only Torah, which helps a person when young and when old, like Avraham Avinu.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: an unmarried man should not herd animals,
chunks.st: A bachelor may not herd cattle,

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִישְׁנוּ שְׁנֵי רַוָּקִים בְּטַלִּית אֶחָת.
chunks.en: and two unmarried men should not sleep under one blanket.
chunks.st: nor may two bachelors sleep with one covering,
chunks.stMore: lest they transgress the prohibition against homosexual intercourse,

chunks.en: But the Sages allow it.
chunks.st: but the Rabbis permit it.

chunks.en: Anyone whose work is with women
chunks.st: Anyone who has professional dealings primarily with women

chunks.en: should not be alone with women.
chunks.st: may not be secluded with women.
chunks.stMore: There is more of a concern that such a man might sin due to his familiarity with the women.

chunks.he: וְלֹא יְלַמֵּד אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ אֻמָּנוּת
chunks.en: And a person should not teach his son a job
chunks.st: And a person may not teach his son a trade

chunks.en: among women.
chunks.st: that necessitates frequent interaction with women, for the same reason.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: With regard to teaching one’s son a trade, Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: A person should always teach his son
chunks.st: A person should always teach his son

chunks.en: a clean and easy job,
chunks.st: a clean and easy trade

chunks.en: and daven to the One Who owns all wealth and property,
chunks.st: and pray for success to the One to Whom wealth and property belong,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין אֻמָּנוּת שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ עֲנִיּוּת וַעֲשִׁירוּת,
chunks.en: because there is no job without being poor and being rich.
chunks.explain: Any job can make a person rich or poor.
chunks.st: as ultimately there is no trade that does not include both poverty and wealth,
chunks.stMore: since a person can become rich from any profession.

chunks.en: Being poor does not come from the job,
chunks.st: Poverty does not come from a particular trade,

chunks.en: and being rich does not come from the job,
chunks.st: nor does wealth come from a particular trade,

chunks.en: but everything goes by a person's merit.
chunks.st: but rather, all is in accordance with a person’s merit.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, one should choose a clean and easy trade, and pray to God for success.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

chunks.en: Did you ever see a wild animal or a bird
chunks.st: Have you ever seen a beast or a bird

chunks.en: that has a job?
chunks.st: that has a trade?

chunks.en: And they get their food without pain.
chunks.st: And yet they earn their livelihood without anguish.

chunks.en: And they were created only to serve me,
chunks.st: But all these were created only to serve me,

chunks.en: and I was created to serve my Maker.
chunks.st: and I, a human being, was created to serve the One Who formed me.

chunks.en: Is it not right that I should get my food without pain?
chunks.st: Is it not right that I should earn my livelihood without anguish?

words.en: that I will get my food

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁהֲרֵעוֹתִי מַעֲשַׂי וְקִפַּחְתִּי אֶת פַּרְנָסָתִי.
chunks.en: But I made my deeds bad, and I lost my easy living.
chunks.st: But I, i.e., humanity, have committed evil actions and have lost my livelihood.
chunks.stMore: This is why people must work to earn a living.

chunks.en: Abba Gurion from Tzadyan
chunks.st: Abba Guryan of Tzadyan

chunks.en: says in the name of Abba Gurya,
chunks.st: says in the name of Abba Gurya:

chunks.en: A person should not teach his son to be
chunks.st: A person may not teach his son

chunks.en: a donkey driver, a camel driver,
chunks.st: the trades of a donkey driver, a camel driver,

chunks.en: a potter, a sailor,
chunks.st: a pot maker, a sailor,

chunks.en: a shepherd, or a storekeeper,
chunks.st: a shepherd, or a storekeeper.

chunks.en: because their jobs are the jobs of robbers.
chunks.explain: These jobs can easily lead to taking what is not yours.
chunks.st: The reason for all these is the same, as their trades are the trades of robbers;
chunks.stMore: all of these professions involve a measure of dishonesty and are likely to lead to robbery.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says in his name,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says in Abba Gurya’s name:

chunks.en: Most donkey drivers are wicked,
chunks.st: Most donkey drivers are wicked, since they engage in deceit,

chunks.en: and most camel drivers are good people.
chunks.explain: They travel in dangerous places and daven to Hashem.
chunks.st: and most camel drivers, who traverse dangerous places such as deserts, are of fit character, as they pray to God to protect them on their journeys.

chunks.en: Most sailors are pious.
chunks.explain: The danger of the sea makes them fear Hashem.
chunks.st: Most sailors are pious, since the great danger of the seas instills in them the fear of Heaven.

chunks.en: The best of doctors goes to Gehinnom.
chunks.st: The best of doctors is to Gehenna,

chunks.en: And the most kosher of butchers
chunks.st: and even the fittest of butchers

chunks.en: is a partner of Amalek.
chunks.st: is a partner of Amalek.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nehorai says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Nehorai says:

chunks.en: I put aside every job in the world,
chunks.st: I set aside all the trades in the world,

chunks.he: וְאֵינִי מְלַמֵּד אֶת בְּנִי אֶלָּא תוֹרָה,
chunks.en: and I teach my son only Torah,
chunks.st: and I teach my son only Torah,

chunks.en: because a person eats from its reward in this world,
chunks.st: as a person partakes of its reward in this world

chunks.en: and the main reward stays for the World to Come.
chunks.st: and the principal reward remains for him in the World-to-Come,

chunks.en: And all other jobs are not like that.
chunks.st: which is not true of other professions, whose rewards are only in this world.

chunks.en: When a person becomes sick,
chunks.st: Furthermore, if a person comes to be ill,

chunks.en: or old,
chunks.st: or old,

chunks.en: or has suffering,
chunks.st: or undergoes suffering,

chunks.en: and he cannot do his work,
chunks.st: and is unable to be involved in his trade,

chunks.en: he dies of hunger.
chunks.st: behold, he dies in hunger.

chunks.en: But Torah is not like that.
chunks.explain: A person can learn Torah at any time.
chunks.st: But with regard to the Torah it is not so, since one can study it under all circumstances.

chunks.en: It guards him from all bad when he is young,
chunks.st: Rather, it preserves him from all evil and sin in his youth,

chunks.en: and gives him a future and hope when he is old.
chunks.st: and provides him with a future and hope in his old age.

chunks.en: About his youth, what does it say?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: With regard to his youth, what does it say about a Torah scholar?

chunks.en: (Yeshayahu 40) Those who hope to Hashem will have new strength.
chunks.st: “But they that wait for the Lord shall renew their strength” (Isaiah 40:31).

chunks.en: About his old age, what does it say?
chunks.st: With regard to his old age, what does it say?

chunks.en: (Tehillim 92) They will still give fruit in old age.
chunks.st: “They shall still bring forth fruit in old age” (Psalms 92:15),

chunks.he: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
chunks.en: And so it says about Avraham Avinu, may he rest in peace,
chunks.st: and it likewise states with regard to Abraham our forefather:

chunks.en: (Bereishis 24) And Avraham was old,
chunks.st: “And Abraham was old,

chunks.en: and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything.
chunks.st: well stricken in age; and the Lord had blessed Abraham in all things” (Genesis 24:1).

chunks.en: We find that Avraham Avinu kept
chunks.st: We found that Abraham our forefather

chunks.he: אֶת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה,
chunks.en: the whole Torah before it was given,
chunks.st: fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given,

chunks.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, (שם כו) עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם
chunks.en: as it says (there 26): Because Avraham listened
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Because that Abraham listened

chunks.he: בְּקֹלִי וַיִּשְׁמֹר מִשְׁמַרְתִּי מִצְוֹתַי חֻקּוֹתַי וְתוֹרֹתָי:
chunks.en: to My voice, and kept My watch, My mitzvos, My laws, and My teachings.
chunks.st: to My voice, and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws” (Genesis 26:5),
chunks.stMore: which indicates that Abraham observed all the mitzvot of his own accord and was rewarded in his old age as a result.
